A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sim-OPRL research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original Star MDP, Gridworld, and sepsis simulation experiments, including sample complexity, policy returns, ablations, and model-accuracy analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds MiniGrid and HalfCheetah results, including dataset-quality analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes candidate-policy membership from optimality for every reward model to optimality for at least one. This corrects the formal selection rule; both versions' practical implementation already maintains one policy per reward-ensemble member. The pessimistic objective and simulated-rollout acquisition procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds MiniGrid-FourRooms navigation and HalfCheetah continuous-control evaluations, including Random, Medium, and Medium-Expert datasets. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's Star MDP, Gridworld, and sepsis simulations.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain OPRL Uniform, OPRL Uncertainty, and online PbOP, alongside optimal-policy reference bounds. Newly discussed methods such as MoP-RL appear in related-work comparisons without empirical evaluation.

E3.justification: New benchmark configurations include PPO for MiniGrid and SAC with five-layer models for HalfCheetah (Appendix C). Appendix E adds evaluation at a fixed budget of 30 preferences. The retained experiments continue using normalized returns and a target suboptimality gap of 20.

E4.justification: The existing Star-MDP ablations and dataset-size, coverage, and model-accuracy analyses are retained. Appendix E adds HalfCheetah sensitivity to dataset optimality, measuring both preferences needed to reach the target and returns under a fixed preference budget.

E5.justification: Table 2 and corresponding main-text plots change their stated experiment count from 20 to 6, while retaining means and 95% confidence intervals. Appendix Figure 7 still reports 20 experiments. These are reporting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether the underlying runs were reduced or the captions corrected.

E6.justification: v2 adds MiniGrid and HalfCheetah results, including Tables 5–6. Table 2 replaces sepsis estimates: Sim-OPRL changes from 830 ± 88 to 225 ± 46 preferences, while OPRL Uniform changes from 18,856 ± 427 to a failure marker. Star-MDP and Gridworld rows remain unchanged. The sepsis revisions are not established as same-setting algorithmic gains.

T1.justification: The main bounds remain unchanged, but v2 corrects the linear-class example to bound log N and repairs Appendix A.3's confusion between value and suboptimality. Mathematical cleanup is incomplete: Algorithm 2's quantifier correction is absent from Lemma A.9, and Equation (10) introduces a square root into the squared-error bound absent from v1 Equation (8), without changing the following uncertainty rate.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the offline preference-elicitation formulation, Sim-OPRL's combination of pessimism and optimism, coverage-dependent sample-complexity guarantees, and superior preference efficiency over OPRL. The reorganized contribution list and broader experiments do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes exact-optimization theoretical guarantees from practical approximations and adds possible language-model alignment applications in Appendix B. It removes v1's explanation of the large sepsis preference requirement through sparse rewards and its proposed proxy-reward warm start. The broader-impact limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents architectures and optimizers for the added benchmarks, D4RL dataset identifiers, and detailed sepsis transition rules in Table 4. Most existing training, ensemble, hardware, and runtime information is retained. Section 6.3 largely expands material already present in v1's implementation appendix.

R1.justification: New Appendix B substantially broadens positioning against preference-based deep RL, alternative elicitation methods, and language-model alignment research. Table 3 adds a detailed taxonomy. Table 1 adds MoP-RL and replaces the efficient-sampling criterion with policy-based sampling, sharpening the distinction underlying the contribution.

P1.justification: The main section order and much existing prose remain intact. Targeted restructuring separates practical implementation into Section 6.3, reorganizes the experimental narrative, and moves the Star-MDP explanation into the environment appendix. Contributions, affiliations, terminology, and citation presentation also receive edits.

P2.justification: v2 consolidates benchmark curves into a five-panel Figure 1, separates the ablations into Figure 2, redraws Figure 3, and combines the Star-MDP illustrations in appendix Figure 5. It expands Table 2 and adds Tables 3–6, substantially changing the visual organization alongside the conference layout.

improvement.justification: The added continuous-control and navigation evaluations, together with HalfCheetah dataset-quality analyses, provide stronger support for applicability beyond v1's evaluations. Clearer implementation exposition and the corrected counterexample also help. These gains are tempered by unexplained sepsis result revisions, changed reported run counts, and incomplete mathematical cleanup, particularly Appendix Equation (10).
